selectedMssDirection.statement: For the current common exact signed-parity realization, canonical capacity-role indices and exact/depth-parity indices are unnecessary. The carrier retains owner separation and signed counts of odd-magnitude changed coordinates in C, D0, and D1.

findings.statement: C_ROLELESS is present in the inclusion-minimal common exact grid point for both SIGN and SIGNED_PARITY. Exact canonical role index i on C:i is therefore unnecessary in the tested common scalar exchange realization.

Under SIGNED_PARITY, D_DEPTHLESS is common-exact on all three hard carriers. Exact frontier-relative depth and depth parity can both be removed while retaining D0/D1 owner separation and signed counts.
Under SIGN, C_ROLELESS+D_DEPTHLESS loses one structural direction and leaves one scalar contradiction on 6x3-k3; depth parity restores exactness. This distinction disappears under SIGNED_PARITY.
The current smallest frozen common role/depth grid point is SIGNED_PARITY with roleless capacity changes plus depthless owner-separated D0/D1 changes.
On 4x5-k4, SIGNED_PARITY C_ROLELESS+D_DEPTHLESS has rank 262 versus full C+D0+D1 signed-parity rank 282, removing twenty structural directions while preserving the two-dimensional scalar image.

After deleting W, capacity role indices, and depth indices, owner separation D0 versus D1 is the major remaining named coordinate distinction in the common signed-parity exchange carrier and is the next lawful MSS target.

nextQuestion: Can D0 and D1 be merged or reduced to symmetric/antisymmetric owner-channel combinations inside the roleless/depthless SIGNED_PARITY exchange carrier, and can the resulting structural image be reduced to the two scalar syndromes?
nonclaims: Roleless/depthless SIGNED_PARITY is not proved globally minimal outside the frozen EW-RS-073 grid.
D0 and D1 are not yet shown individually necessary or mergeable.
No individual exchange key or scalar coefficient is promoted as invariant.
EW-RS-059 PRIMARY 3x6-k4 and BACKUP 5x3-k4 remain sealed.
No Q-A/Q-F, standard-7x6, universal theorem, or center-opening proof follows.
